title: Peripheral intravenous catheter failure before and after a change to clinically indicated replacement: a cohort study using routinely collected data
abstract: Objective: to estimate whether a change from routine resiting every 96 hours to clinically indicated replacement was associated with more catheter failure on adult medical and surgical wards. Design: cohort of all catheters inserted in the 12 months before and after 1 March 2025, from flowsheet and surveillance records. Outcome: removal for phlebitis, infiltration, occlusion or dislodgement before the end of treatment. Analysis: cause-specific Cox model with a patient frailty term and an interrupted time series. Results and conclusions will be written after the analysis.
introduction: Clinically indicated replacement reduces insertions without more phlebitis in published comparisons, but results after local policy changes vary and few analyses account for patients with several catheters. Ward nurses disagree about the effect of the change here, and two bloodstream infections have raised concern.
methods: Existing flowsheet records for catheters inserted from 1 March 2024 to 28 February 2026 are linked to admissions and infection surveillance. Removal reasons are coded with a rule fixed in advance and checked on a random sample. The primary model accounts for competing removal and for several catheters per patient; a segmented regression of monthly failure addresses secular trends.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present the cohort flow, catheters per patient, failure by period with the adjusted hazard ratio and absolute difference, the monthly time series, catheters per admission, infection counts and documentation completeness.
discussion: The discussion will weigh the local estimate against published comparisons, the time series and the co-intervention list, and state what the result means for the policy.
limitations: Before-after design open to secular trends; documentation may differ between periods; infections too rare to compare; visual phlebitis scoring.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will be limited to failure and insertions in this hospital and will not claim an effect on bloodstream infection.
summary: STROBE and RECORD structured draft with results left empty until analysis.
